bodyMarkdown:
## Tram Driver Salary Melbourne: Base Rates and What You Actually Earn

If you are researching the **tram driver salary Melbourne**, the first thing to know is that Melbourne's tram drivers are employed by Yarra Trams under a specific enterprise agreement approved by the Fair Work Commission. Their pay is not set by the Road Transport and Distribution Award that covers many other transport workers. This article explains the base rates, the effect of penalty rates, and how to convert an hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and take-home pay.

### Base Rates Under the Yarra Trams Enterprise Agreement

From the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026, a qualified Yarra Trams driver at Level 3 (after one year of service) earns **$1,840.29 per week** for 38 ordinary hours. That works out to **$48.43 per hour** and an annual base salary of **$95,695** (weekly rate × 52). Drivers with 20 years of service (Level 4) earn $1,863.08 per week ($96,880 per year). Trainees start at $1,545.76 per week ($40.68 per hour) for the first nine months.

These rates are before any shift penalties, weekend loadings, or overtime. The enterprise agreement also includes a further 1% increase once the Next Generation Trams are introduced, which would lift the Level 3 rate to $1,858.69 per week.

### How Penalty Rates Boost the Tram Driver Salary Melbourne

Tram drivers work rotating rosters that include early mornings, nights, and weekends. The Yarra Trams agreement provides:
- Saturday work: time and a half (1.5×)
- Sunday work: double time (2×), minimum four hours
- Public holidays: double time and a half (2.5×)
- Overtime: time and a half for the first 3 hours, double time thereafter

Because of these penalties, the actual **tram driver salary Melbourne** is often higher than the base rate. The Australian Taxation Office's Taxation Statistics for 2023–24 show a median salary or wage of **$102,579** for the 1,719 tram drivers who lodged tax returns. That figure includes part-time and casual workers, so full-time drivers with regular penalties likely earn more than the median. The ATO data is more reliable than recruiter surveys such as Glassdoor, which reported an average base pay of $80,000 for Melbourne tram drivers in October 2026. The ATO figure reflects what people actually earned, including penalties and overtime.

### Converting Hourly Rates to Annual and Fortnightly Pay

To estimate your annual salary from an hourly rate, use the formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a full-time tram driver, the standard week is 38 hours. For example:
- $48.43 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $95,695 per year
- Fortnightly base pay: $1,840.29 × 2 = $3,680.58 before tax

If you are a casual employee (though Yarra Trams does not employ casual drivers under its agreement), you would add 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your hourly rate and toggle casual loading to see the difference.

### Comparing Tram Driver Pay to Award Rates and the Minimum Wage

The national minimum wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). A qualified Yarra Trams driver earns 83% more than that at base rate. Even a trainee tram driver at $40.68 per hour is well above the minimum.

For context, the Road Transport and Distribution Award (which does not cover tram drivers) sets minimum rates for transport workers from $26.87 per hour (Grade 1) to $29.42 per hour (Grade 7) as of July 2026. Tram drivers under the enterprise agreement earn significantly more than these award rates.

### Take-Home Pay, Tax, and Superannuation

Using the base annual salary of $95,695 for a qualified Yarra Trams driver, we can estimate take-home pay for 2026–27:
- Income tax: approximately $19,500 (using the resident tax scale: nil to $18,200, 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000)
- Medicare levy: 2% of taxable income, about $1,914
- Net annual take-home: about $74,500
- Fortnightly take-home: about $2,867

Superannuation is paid on top of the base salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $95,695 salary, that adds **$11,483 per year** to your retirement savings, not to your take-home pay. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrifice can affect your tax.

### What About Adelaide Tram Drivers?

For comparison, Adelaide Metro tram operators earn lower base rates. A qualified tram operator in Adelaide gets $1,511.99 per week ($78,623 per year) from January 2026, with no further increases until a new agreement is reached. The Melbourne tram driver salary is therefore about 22% higher at base rate.

### Key Takeaways

- The **tram driver salary Melbourne** base rate for a qualified driver is $95,695 per year from July 2026.
- With penalties and overtime, the ATO median is $102,579.
- Always convert hourly rates using 38 hours per week for full-time work.
- Super is 12% on top of ordinary earnings, not deducted from your pay.
- For a personalised estimate, use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool or the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) guide.
